# Test synthesis and acceptance

Status: **proposed (M1)**. Decisions: QD4, QD5, QD6.

## Emitter (MT-6.1)

`emitSpec(trajectory: Trajectory, options): string` in `src/synth/emit.ts`. Pure
function, no I/O, no model. Same input → byte-identical output. Snapshot-tested.

Output shape:

```ts
// Generated by magpi-test from trajectory create-invoice-custom-address--1.
// Do not edit by hand: change the scenario or trajectory and regenerate.
import { test, expect } from "@playwright/test";

test("Create invoice with a custom payout address", async ({ page }) => {
  await test.step("open the create page", async () => {
    await page.goto("/create");
  });
  await test.step("choose custom payout address", async () => {
    await page.getByRole("radio", { name: "Custom address", exact: true }).click();
  });
  await test.step("enter the payout address", async () => {
    await page.getByLabel("Payout address", { exact: true }).fill("0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111");
  });
  await test.step("create the invoice", async () => {
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Create invoice", exact: true }).click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/pay/);
  });
  await expect(page.getByText("25", { exact: false }).first()).toBeVisible();
});
```

Rules:

- One file per accepted trajectory: `magpi-tests/specs/<scenarioId>.spec.ts`.
- Strings are emitted with `JSON.stringify`, never concatenated into code.
- `test.step` titles are the step `intent`, trimmed to 80 chars.
- No `waitForTimeout`, no `sleep`. Waiting is done by web-first assertions and
  `toHaveURL`.
- No `page.locator(css)`, no XPath, no `data-core-ref`.
- `{ env: "X" }` emits `process.env.X ?? ""` and the spec fails fast with a clear
  message if empty. `{ unique: "invoice-{n}" }` emits a value built from
  `test.info().testId` and `Date.now()`.

## Target → locator

| Target | Playwright |
| --- | --- |
| `{by:"role", role, name, exact}` | `page.getByRole(role, { name, exact })` |
| `{by:"label", text, exact}` | `page.getByLabel(text, { exact })` |
| `{by:"placeholder", text}` | `page.getByPlaceholder(text)` |
| `{by:"text", text, exact}` | `page.getByText(text, { exact })` |
| `{by:"testId", id}` | `page.getByTestId(id)` |

Preference when the repair loop must pick a different target for the same element:
`testId` (only if the app has one) > `role+name` > `label` > `placeholder` > `text`.
This is Playwright's own recommendation. Before writing a locator picker of our own,
MT-0.1 checks whether Playwright's selector generator (used by `codegen` and the
`pick locator` tool) can be called from code; if so, use it in the repair loop.

## Predicate → assertion

| Predicate | Playwright |
| --- | --- |
| `url_includes {text}` | `await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(escapeRegex(text)))` |
| `title_includes {text}` | `await expect(page).toHaveTitle(new RegExp(escapeRegex(text)))` |
| `text_visible {text}` | `await expect(page.getByText(text).first()).toBeVisible()` |
| `text_absent {text}` | `await expect(page.getByText(text)).toHaveCount(0)` |
| `control_exists {role,name}` | `await expect(page.getByRole(role, { name }).first()).toBeVisible()` |
| `control_absent {role,name}` | `await expect(page.getByRole(role, { name })).toHaveCount(0)` |
| `value_equals {name,text}` | `await expect(page.getByLabel(name)).toHaveValue(text)` |
| `value_includes {name,text}` | `await expect(page.getByLabel(name)).toHaveValue(new RegExp(escapeRegex(text)))` |
| `no_console_error` | collect `page.on("console")` errors from test start; `expect(errors).toEqual([])` at the end |
| `dialog_open {open}` | `await expect(page.getByRole("dialog")).toBeVisible()` / `.toHaveCount(0)` |
| `all {of}` | each assertion in order |
| `any`, `not` | not supported by the M1 emitter: fail synthesis with a clear error; the scenario must be rewritten |

`control_exists` with only `role` or only `name` is allowed; emit what is present.

## Dynamic values

Never assert values that change per run: addresses, invoice ids, transaction hashes,
timestamps, generated names. When building `waitFor` and when the criteria compiler
writes criteria:

- replace path segments that look like ids (hex `0x…`, UUIDs, long digit or base58
  runs) with a regex wildcard, or keep only the stable prefix (`/pay`);
- drop query strings unless the scenario names a parameter;
- for text, assert the stable label ("Invoice created") rather than the value next to
  it.

## Generated config (MT-6.2)

`magpi-tests/playwright.config.ts`:

```ts
import base from "../playwright.config";
import { defineConfig } from "@playwright/test";
import path from "node:path";

const root = path.resolve(__dirname, "..");
const servers = base.webServer ? [base.webServer].flat() : [];

export default defineConfig({
  ...base,
  testDir: "./specs",
  retries: 0,
  use: { ...base.use, locale: "en-US", trace: "retain-on-failure" },
  webServer: servers.map((s) => ({ ...s, cwd: s.cwd ?? root })),
});
```

The `cwd` fix matters: Playwright runs `webServer.command` from the config file's
directory, and onchain-invoice's commands (`node ui/e2e/stack/boot.mjs`) are relative
to the repo root. If the target has ESM-only config semantics where `__dirname` is not
defined, use `fileURLToPath(new URL("..", import.meta.url))`; MT-6.2 checks which.
If the target has no Playwright config, emit a standalone config with `baseURL` and
`webServer` built from the manifest's `processes`.

## Acceptance (MT-6.3)

```bash
CI=1 npx playwright test --config magpi-tests/playwright.config.ts \
  magpi-tests/specs/<id>.spec.ts --repeat-each=3 --retries=0 --workers=1 \
  --reporter=json
```

- Runs from the target root. Stop the exploration stack first: `CI=1` disables
  `reuseExistingServer`, so ports must be free and the stack starts fresh.
- Write candidates to `magpi-tests/state/pending/<id>.spec.ts` and move them into
  `specs/` only after 3/3 pass.
- Parse the JSON reporter output, not stdout text.
- Classify a failure as one of: `locator` (strict mode violation, element not found),
  `assertion` (expect failed), `timeout`, `environment` (webServer failed to start, port
  in use), `other`. Only `locator` and `assertion` go to repair. `environment` stops
  the batch: the next specs would fail for the same reason.
- To save time, acceptance may batch several pending specs in one Playwright
  invocation; a spec is accepted only if all 3 of its repeats pass.

## Repair loop (MT-6.4)

Up to 2 repair attempts per trajectory. Input to the model, and nothing else:

- the trajectory JSON;
- the failing step index and the Playwright error message (first 40 lines);
- an ARIA snapshot of the page at failure (`await page.locator("body").ariaSnapshot()`
  captured by a small helper run, or from the trace), trimmed to 200 lines.

Output: a JSON patch-like list of changes to `steps[i].action.target`, `steps[i].waitFor`,
or `steps[i].action.value`. The repair loop must not change `assertions` (those are the
scenario's criteria; changing them would be grading itself). If the assertion itself is
wrong, quarantine and record `suspected: "criteria"` for a human; if the app looks
broken, record `suspected: "product-bug"`.

## No-AI guard (MT-6.5)

A check run before acceptance and in `npm test` over fixture output:

- every generated spec's imports ⊆ `@playwright/test`, `node:*`, and
  `fixtures.allowedImports`;
- the file contains none of: `magpi` (outside the header comment), `browser-agent`,
  `openrouter`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `fetch(`, `API_KEY`;
- the emitted header comment is present.
